name: OGRF Garrison — Cobasna Ammunition Depot
detail: Roughly 1,500-strong Operational Group of Russian Forces contingent guarding the Soviet-era Cobasna depot's estimated 19,000-22,000 tonnes of munitions, 2km from the Ukrainian border. Core command (~70-100 Russian officers) was declared persona non grata by Chisinau on April 17, 2026.

name: Cuciurgan Power Station (Moldavskaya GRES / MGRES)
detail: Transnistria's dominant power plant, historically fuelled by free Russian gas and supplying up to 80% of Moldova's electricity. Switched to coal in February 2026 amid gas-supply instability; now supplemented by Moldovagaz-brokered gas via MET Group.

name: Moldovan Army Air Operations Service
detail: National radar and airspace-monitoring service responsible for detecting and reporting drone incursions, including the August 10 Priozerne crossing detected at 23:41 local time and the wave of five drone crossings tracked across the Ștefan Vodă frontier between 03:56 and 06:02 on August 27.

name: NATO Air Policing Detachment, Romania (incl. Spanish F/A-18s)
detail: Rotating NATO fighter detachment flying Air Policing missions over Romanian airspace bordering Moldova; a Spanish F/A-18 Hornet shot down a Shahed-136/Geran-2-type drone near Galați on August 16, 2026. Two Romanian F-16s and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter from the 86th Air Base at Borcea scrambled on August 24 after a drone crossed via Moldova's Vulcănești and entered Romanian airspace toward Vrancea County.

name: Moldova-Romania High-Voltage Electricity Interconnector
detail: New high-voltage link completed around May 2026 under a EUR 270 million EU/EIB/EBRD/World Bank package, reducing Moldova's reliance on Cuciurgan-generated electricity; two further interconnectors planned for 2027 and 2029.

name: Moldovan Intelligence and Security Service (SIS)
detail: National security and intelligence agency responsible for counter-hybrid-threat assessments, including monitoring of passportisation, disinformation and vote-buying operations linked to the Shor network.

name: Tiraspoltransgaz Gas Transit Network
detail: Transnistrian gas transmission and metering infrastructure through which Moldovagaz-brokered supply (via Swiss-based MET Group) has flowed to Cuciurgan since February 2025, replacing the free Russian gas cut off in January 2025.

name: EU Reform and Growth Facility for Moldova
detail: EUR 1.9 billion (2025-2027) EU financial instrument combining EUR 385 million in grants and up to EUR 1.5 billion in concessional loans, conditioned on reform benchmarks; roughly EUR 504 million disbursed as of mid-2026, underpinning Moldova's energy-diversification and reform agenda.
